title: At the table
subtitle: Serving and pairing Pinot Gris
objectives: Know how long to keep it

steps.title: Match the style
steps.body: Light Pinot Grigio suits aperitifs, salads, light seafood and simple pasta. Rich Pinot Gris suits roast pork, chicken, smoked fish, mushroom dishes and mildly spiced Asian food. Ramato suits charcuterie, risotto and grilled fish. Off-dry Alsace Pinot Gris suits foie gras.
steps.highlight: Grigio light; Gris with richer food

steps.title: Service and age
steps.body: Serve Pinot Grigio at 7 to 9 degrees, Pinot Gris and ramato at 10 to 12. Most Pinot Grigio is best within a year or two. Alsace Grand Cru Pinot Gris can age 10 years or more, developing honey and smoke.
steps.highlight: Grigio young; Grand Cru Gris ages

steps.prompt: Which dish suits a rich Alsace Pinot Gris?
steps.explanation: Rich Pinot Gris matches pork and fruit.

steps.body: An off-dry Alsace Pinot Gris with smoked salmon or a lightly spiced Thai dish brings out its ginger and smoky notes.

steps.prompt: Most Pinot Grigio is made for long ageing.
steps.explanation: Not true. It's best young and fresh.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Pinot Grigio suits light food; Pinot Gris richer dishes
Grand Cru Pinot Gris can age 10 years or more
